tables.title: Blob creation steps for scalar multiplication (CCOP = 0b100000<i>0)
tables.text: Table 192, "Blob creation steps for scalar multiplication (CCOP = 0b100000<i>0)", in section 25.5.3 (ECC scalar multiplication) on page 763. Columns: OPSTEP, inM OPDKEA, iGn CSMAPEHS, Coupling or chaining operations, End-step (1)event, CPU action in step. 10 data row(s). Notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.; 2. Once START bit is set SAES is reset, and OPERR linked to SAES are deactivated. Also when.

rows:
–Enable the PKA in the correct mode, writing in 
PKA_CR MODE= 0x20 and EN=1 (repeat if EN bit 
stays clear). Wait for INITOK=1 in PKA_SR.
–Optionally decrypt blob encryption key in the SAES, 
using DHUK in 256-bit wrapped key mode.
–Set up AES-GCM in 256-bit encryption mode 
withDHUK or the decrypted key in register 
(ifapplicable)
–Write base point G coordinates as input in PKA RAM.

–Complete GCM initialization in encryption mode. 
Registers IVR1 to 3 are loaded with randoms.
–Read back blob IV in IVR registers.

Write ECC scalar multiplication parameters in the PKA 
RAM, clearing CCF flags in SAES, triggered after each 
64-bitwrite.

Write incrementally k in the PKA, using 0xCCB magic 
number. Values are drawn from the RNG. The PKA runs 
a special sanity check to verify random compliance with 
NIST standard (RNGERRF is set if the sanity check 
fails).
Write incrementally k in the PKA.

–Read incrementally k from the PKA (writing 0xCCB 
magic numbers), and runs AES encryption rounds.
–Read encrypted k in SAES DOUTR. 
–Repeat for each 16-byte block of data..

– Complete GCM final.
–Read reference tag in the SAES.
–Start the operation in PKA setting START bit in 
PKA_CR
For the first two steps keep the SAES enabled (EN bit 
set).
The PKA computes the operation, PKA RAM reads as 0

–Read reference public key point Q in PKA RAM, and 
save it in SRAM to verify the new blob.
–Set IPRST in CCB.

Clear the IPRST bit in CCB when CCB_BUSY and 
OPSTEP are cleared in CCB_SR.
notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.
2. Once START bit is set SAES is reset, and OPERR linked to SAES are deactivated. Also when START bit is set, CCB sets OPSTEP to 0x19 after a few cycles.
3. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.
